title: New LEGO Architecture Tower Bridge compared to the 2010 classic
summary: An early review from Cheesey Studios lines up the upcoming 21067 Tower Bridge against the 2010 original, revealing size, detail and functionality differences.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Ahead of its full release, early reviews of LEGO Architecture 21067 Tower Bridge are starting to appear, including a detailed side-by-side comparison with the 2010 set 10214 Tower Bridge from reviewer Cheesey Studios.

Despite having only around 300 more pieces than the original, the new 21067 model is reportedly about 25% smaller overall. This is put down to the use of newer, smaller detail pieces that let designers achieve a more proportionally accurate bridge shape than was possible back in 2010, when the middle section had to be compressed to keep the model a manageable size for display.

The comparison also points out that although the instructions reference the real bridge's ability to open, the new 21067 model apparently can't fully open, unlike the older 10214 version. The extra detail in the new set may be a factor here.

Another difference flagged is how the windows are handled: the larger 2010 set uses brick-built windows, while the smaller 2026 version uses printed decorated elements instead. These prints are said to be useful for other builds thanks to being on tiles, but they can stick out slightly from the model's structure.

## Why it matters
For Tower Bridge fans and Architecture line collectors, this comparison gives a useful early look at how LEGO design techniques have evolved over 16 years, and highlights a genuine trade-off between size, accuracy and playable/display features when choosing between the two versions.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for further official reviews and confirmed details on 21067 Tower Bridge as more coverage and hands-on builds emerge closer to release.

title: Why LEGO Ideas 21372 La Catrina Skips Printed Skull Details
summary: LEGO designers have explained why the new LEGO Ideas 21372 La Catrina set leaves its skull unprinted, unlike the earlier BrickHeadz version — and it comes down to cultural accuracy rather than cost-cutting.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics sat down with the LEGO design team behind LEGO Ideas 21372 La Catrina and asked why the set's skull piece has no printed decoration, unlike the retired 40492 La Catrina BrickHeadz, which featured painted skull detailing.

Designer Jim Clayton and LEGO Ideas Creative Lead Jordan Scott said the team went back and forth on whether to add printing, exploring several variants along the way. It was Graphic Designer Melody Flores, drawing on her own experience with Day of the Dead traditions, who made the case for leaving the skull plain. Her point: La Catrina is fundamentally a skull figure — the Lady of Death — and doesn't need extra decoration to be recognisable or authentic.

Instead, the team put decorative effort into skull patterns printed on La Catrina's dress, giving the model detail elsewhere while keeping the skull itself true to how the character is traditionally depicted.

## Why it matters
It's a good reminder that design choices on LEGO sets aren't always about budget — sometimes they're deliberate calls rooted in getting cultural representation right. For collectors comparing 21372 La Catrina to the older BrickHeadz version, this explains the visual difference and adds some welcome context to a set inspired by a significant cultural figure.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for further details from LEGO's design team roundtable, including more on the dress printing and other design decisions behind 21372 La Catrina.

title: LEGO Art reveals 31221 Gustav Klimt – The Kiss, but does it beat the gold record?
summary: LEGO has officially unveiled a 4,000-piece LEGO Art recreation of Gustav Klimt's The Kiss, arriving 1 August, though it's not yet clear if it beats 31213 Mona Lisa's record for most metallic gold pieces in a set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially unveiled 31221 Gustav Klimt – The Kiss, the latest addition to the LEGO Art theme. The 4,000-piece build releases on 1 August and recreates the famous Austrian painting using multiple metallic gold elements, echoing the Byzantine mosaic and Japanese lacquer techniques Klimt drew on for the original artwork.

What's still unconfirmed is exactly how many metallic gold pieces the set contains. That matters because LEGO Art has quietly built up a bit of a gold-piece leaderboard over the years. The soon-to-retire 31213 Mona Lisa currently holds the record with 314 metallic gold pieces out of 1,503 total, all used in the frame around Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece. Before that, 2021's 76191 Infinity Gauntlet included 153 gold pieces, and 2020's 80012 Monkey King Warrior Mech had 119.

With The Kiss's much larger 4,000-piece count and gold being central to Klimt's original technique, there's plenty of reason to think it could challenge Mona Lisa's crown — but until LEGO confirms the breakdown, that's speculation.

## Why it matters
For collectors and display builders, metallic gold elements are prized both for their rarity and their striking look on a shelf. A new record-holder would be a notable moment for the LEGO Art theme and could affect demand and resale interest, especially with Mona Lisa retiring soon.

## What to watch next
Expect the full piece count and gold element breakdown to surface closer to or on the 1 August release date. Worth checking official LEGO channels or Brick Fanatics for confirmation before treating any gold-piece comparison as fact.
